speaker: maya
text: Last time: the Pueblo Revolt — the conquered answering back, and an empire forced to change. Now: no new boxes. Eight episodes, ten questions, eleven minutes. The dare: fit every answer to the unit's three shapes: what changed, what stayed the same, who pushed back. The eight boxes: Native societies, why Europe sailed, the Exchange, Jamestown, the silver mountain, the labor chain, Valladolid, the Pueblo Revolt. Circle the ones you couldn't explain right now.

speaker: jay
text: Ten questions. Any mercy today?

speaker: maya
text: Not a drop of mercy. Question one: three Native regions, and how the land shaped them.

speaker: jay
text: Southwest: Pueblo farmers, adobe, irrigation. Plains: bison hunters, tipis, following the herds. Northeast: mixed farming, hunting, fishing, longhouses.

speaker: maya
text: The engine under all three?

speaker: jay
text: Maize, bred from a wild grass and carried north. No maize, no Cahokia.

speaker: maya
text: Cahokia: ten to twenty thousand at its peak, London-sized, around a hundred-foot mound. The Iroquois?

speaker: jay
text: Five nations, one council, every nation agreeing. Clan mothers chose the leaders.

speaker: maya
text: The myth to drop: the untouched wilderness. Box-one mistake: nobody "found" maize. Scoring move: a big pre-contact city means the follow-up is about food. Clean start.

speaker: maya
text: Question two: what got Europeans across the Atlantic? Motives, then tools.

speaker: jay
text: The three Gs, ranked: gold (spices, silk, the Ottoman squeeze), God (the Reconquista; Granada, January 1492), glory (crowns racing Portugal).

speaker: maya
text: Lead with the economics. The tools?

speaker: jay
text: Caravel, lateen sails, astrolabe, compass, portolan charts, and Henry the Navigator's money. He funded the voyages; the famous school was mostly legend.

speaker: maya
text: The money part was true. The pope's line?

speaker: jay
text: Tordesillas, 1494: three hundred and seventy leagues west of Cape Verde. Spain east, Portugal west —

speaker: maya
text: Flip those two. Spain west, Portugal east, which is why Brazil speaks Portuguese. France and England never signed.

speaker: jay
text: Right. Spain west. Got it.

speaker: maya
text: I drew a line down the middle of a shared bedroom once. It lasted a day. Bonus: why did Spain fund Columbus when Portugal's math said no?

speaker: jay
text: Granada. Fresh off the holy war, desperate to catch Portugal. Four voyages; he died still insisting he'd found Asia.

speaker: maya
text: The box-two mistake: 1492 isn't just Columbus. Both pieces landed.

speaker: maya
text: Question three: the Exchange. Each way, and the deadliest cargo.

speaker: jay
text: West: wheat, sugarcane, horses, cattle, pigs. East: maize, potatoes, tomatoes, tobacco. Deadliest: disease; eight or nine out of ten in the hardest-hit towns.

speaker: maya
text: The one disease that might have gone east?

speaker: jay
text: Syphilis, maybe. Some say it crossed from the Americas; others say it was already in Europe. Nobody's settled it.

speaker: maya
text: Name both sides or it's a trap. Crosby named the swap in 1972: no treaty, no vote, the biggest cargo crossed without a ticket. Who gained on the Native side?

speaker: jay
text: The Plains. The horse. The Comanche rebuilt around it; the horse cultures everyone pictures are post-Exchange. Old, but not ancient.

speaker: maya
text: The box-three mistake: sending the livestock east. They all went west. Locked.

speaker: maya
text: Question four: Jamestown. Why did it almost die?

speaker: jay
text: Private money, on a royal charter: the Virginia Company, 1606. Gentlemen hunting gold in a swamp. Smith's rule held until his gunpowder bag sent him home. Winter 1609: five hundred down to sixty.

speaker: maya
text: Spring of 1610. Then what?

speaker: jay
text: The survivors quit, and sailed into De La Warr, arriving with fresh colonists. He turned them around.

speaker: maya
text: What saved it for good?

speaker: jay
text: Tobacco. Rolfe's Caribbean strain, around 1612. Then the headright: fifty acres to whoever paid the passage.

speaker: maya
text: The planter who paid. And 1619?

speaker: jay
text: The House of Burgesses, and the White Lion landing "20 and odd" Africans at Point Comfort. The vote and the landing, same year.

speaker: maya
text: Then 1622: Opechancanough's attack, 347 dead, a quarter of the colony. Royal colony by 1624. Pair tobacco with a labor system. No misses yet.

speaker: maya
text: Question five: why was Potosi the engine of the Spanish Empire?

speaker: jay
text: The 1545 strike: Huallpa's wind, or the llama. Thirteen thousand feet, a mint at the mountain's foot, Potosi's own pieces of eight. The crown took a fifth.

speaker: maya
text: The quinto, a full fifth. And the town?

speaker: jay
text: Something like 160,000 by the early 1600s, London-sized in the clouds. The labor: the mita, one in seven, mercury on the poorer ore from the 1570s. A forced draft, not slavery.

speaker: maya
text: Don't let an answer choice call it slavery. Who speaks from inside?

speaker: jay
text: Guaman Poma: twelve hundred pages, a letter to the king around 1615. The king never saw it.

speaker: maya
text: Your turn. One mountain, endless silver, the crown borrowing against ships not yet docked. Save it or break it?

speaker: maya
text: It breaks it. Four bankruptcies under Philip the Second. Bodin, 1568: American silver, more money chasing the same goods.

speaker: jay
text: So "inflation" alone won't score.

speaker: maya
text: Write the mechanism. The silver that skipped Spain?

speaker: jay
text: The Manila galleons: silver west, silk east, Urdaneta's way home. The merchants kept most of it.

speaker: maya
text: The box-five mistake: don't sail the silver east. Five down; we're halfway home.

speaker: maya
text: That closes the what-changed half. Question six: what drove each labor shift?

speaker: jay
text: The encomienda: a town's labor and tribute to a colonist. Disease emptied the towns. The New Laws of 1542 tried to kill the inheritance; the encomenderos killed the viceroy at Anaquito in 1546, and the crown caved.

speaker: maya
text: The New Laws didn't end the encomienda; the encomenderos ended the reform. Then?

speaker: jay
text: The drafts: repartimiento in New Spain, the mita in Peru. The crown assigned rotating workers, short stints, wages on paper.

speaker: maya
text: Same idea, two different names.

speaker: jay
text: So Spain scaled up the Portuguese machine: Atlantic sugar islands ran on enslaved African labor. The Middle Passage: thousands, then millions; thirteen out of a hundred died crossing.

speaker: maya
text: The shippers budgeted for the dying. And Las Casas?

speaker: jay
text: In 1516 he proposed African labor instead. He didn't start the trade, but he lent it respectability.

speaker: maya
text: The ladder the labor built?

speaker: jay
text: The casta system: peninsulares, criollos, mestizos, mulatos, Indigenous peoples, Africans. Part custom, part law.

speaker: maya
text: And peninsulares were the American-born ones, right?

speaker: jay
text: Spain. Peninsulares were born in Spain; criollos here. You did the thing you warned me about.

speaker: maya
text: I absolutely did. Behind the ladder: the hacienda, peons free on paper, bound by debt.

speaker: jay
text: Free on paper, chained by the ledger.

speaker: maya
text: The machine just swapped fuel. The ladder holds.

speaker: maya
text: Question seven: Las Casas versus Sepulveda. The actual disagreement?

speaker: jay
text: Fully human with rights, or natural slaves? Las Casas: rational souls, gave back his encomienda in 1514. Sepulveda: Aristotle's four just causes, never crossed the Atlantic.

speaker: maya
text: All from his library: Aristotle, Oviedo's chronicles. The four causes?

speaker: jay
text: Natural slavery. Idolatry offending natural law. Rescuing the innocents. Carrying the faith.

speaker: maya
text: Valladolid, August 1550, again in April 1551. The verdict?

speaker: jay
text: No verdict. Both sides claimed victory.

speaker: maya
text: The box-seven mistake: don't write that either side won. Timing trap: the New Laws came in 1542, so the debate was the crown's second try. The afterlife?

speaker: jay
text: The Short Account, written 1542, printed 1552: the Black Legend in Dutch and English hands, 1578 and 1583. He wrote it to save the Indians; it became Protestant propaganda.

speaker: maya
text: The debate's boxed.

speaker: maya
text: Question eight: the Pueblo Revolt. Causes, and why the winning didn't last.

speaker: jay
text: Eighty years of missions: banned kivas, burned masks, forced labor. Then drought, raids, 1675: Treviño arrests forty-seven medicine men. Pope plans five years from Taos.

speaker: maya
text: And Pope, the Pueblo king?

speaker: jay
text: Holy man; the pueblos never had kings. Knotted cords: maguey fiber, one knot per day. August 10th, 1680, through Spanish pens: Naranjo's account.

speaker: jay
text: Close to four hundred Spaniards dead, twenty-one priests. Santa Fe besieged; Otermin's reports describe the retreat to El Paso, August 21st.

speaker: maya
text: Twelve years free. Why didn't it hold?

speaker: jay
text: Drought, rivalries, Pope turned theocrat — the Spanish called him a tyrant, exactly what you'd expect the losers to write about the winner. Deposed, re-elected in 1688, dead around 1692.

speaker: maya
text: Your turn. You're the crown, 1692. A province walked out for twelve years. Vargas reaches Santa Fe: fight or talk?

speaker: maya
text: He talks: pardons, respect for Pueblo lands, bloodless by Spanish accounts. Then 1693, back with colonists, and it's force. Box-eight mistake: writing that Vargas fought his way in, in 1692. He talked in '92; the force came in '93.

speaker: jay
text: Spain came back scared: land, courts, tolerated ceremonies.

speaker: maya
text: Fear rewrote the rules. That's the revolt, told straight.

speaker: maya
text: Now who pushed back. Question nine: the New Laws and Valladolid both tried to restrain the conquest. Why did so little change?

speaker: jay
text: The machine needed workers; every fix threatened the supply.

speaker: maya
text: And the crown's actions say the money came first. Las Casas won the argument — and it changed nothing on the ground.

speaker: jay
text: So the question outlived the answer.

speaker: maya
text: The pushback's scored.

speaker: maya
text: Last one: why does 1491 to 1607 shape everything after?

speaker: jay
text: Contact created a new world on conquest's terms. The biology, economy, and labor of everything after were decided here.

speaker: maya
text: The period thesis. Ten down.

speaker: maya
text: Eight boxes, let's land them. One: Native societies. Land decided food; food decided the move.

speaker: maya
text: Box one, checked.

speaker: maya
text: Two: why Europe sailed. Gold led, God and glory rode along. Tordesillas: two crowns, everybody else ignored it.

speaker: maya
text: Box two, checked.

speaker: maya
text: Three: the Exchange. Crops and animals both ways, germs one way.

speaker: maya
text: Box three, checked.

speaker: maya
text: Four: Jamestown. Company money, the starving winter, tobacco. 1619: the Burgesses and the White Lion at—

speaker: jay
text: Point Comfort. Don't say Jamestown.

speaker: maya
text: Point Comfort. Jamestown's the trap answer and I almost took it. Box four, checked.

speaker: maya
text: Five: the silver mountain. 1545, the quinto, the mita, Bodin beat Malestroit.

speaker: maya
text: Box five, checked.

speaker: maya
text: Six: the labor chain. The grant, the drafts, the crossing, the ladder.

speaker: maya
text: Box six, checked.

speaker: maya
text: Seven: Valladolid. Four causes from the library, the answer from the field. No verdict.

speaker: maya
text: Box seven, checked.

speaker: maya
text: Eight: the Pueblo Revolt. The cords, 1680, twelve years free. Talked in '92, fought in '93.

speaker: maya
text: Box eight, checked.

speaker: maya
text: Three questions, AP-shaped. Say your answer before I give it.

speaker: maya
text: One, with a source. A planter writes "20 and odd" Africans … "bought for victuals" at Point Comfort, the same year the Burgesses meet. Why pair them?

speaker: maya
text: Self-government and forced labor arrived together — the Burgesses and the White Lion, 1619. The same tobacco economy that needed bound labor also produced planters demanding a say.

speaker: maya
text: Two. "The Treaty of Tordesillas divided the world between Spain and Portugal." What's the mistake?

speaker: maya
text: It bound two crowns, and no one else — France and England never accepted the line, so the line only restrained the two crowns that signed it.

speaker: maya
text: Three. Did Native peoples shape this period, or only get shaped by it?

speaker: maya
text: They shaped it — maize built Cahokia; the horse rebuilt Plains life; the Pueblos held a province twelve years. Pushback is the unit's third shape, and it changed how Spain ruled.

speaker: maya
text: One more, fast. Potosi's draft: mita or repartimiento?

speaker: maya
text: Mita. Peru's. Repartimiento is New Spain's.

speaker: maya
text: Ten questions, eight episodes, one unit —

speaker: jay
text: no mercy, and all of them landed.

speaker: maya
text: Check your eight boxes. Next time: the neighbors move in. Spain, France, Holland, England: four empires, four ways to run a colony.
